questions.q: Which service typically runs its queries over UDP?
questions.solution: A single quick query-and-reply fits **UDP** (port 53); mail, FTP and HTTPS ride on reliable TCP.

questions.q: Digital computers represent all data using —
questions.solution: A **digital** computer converts every input into **discrete binary values (0 and 1)** and computes on them. Continuous quantities are the domain of analog machines.

questions.q:
Match the app to its private-window shortcut:
A. Chrome  B. Edge  C. Firefox
questions.solution: Chrome and Edge (Chromium family) share **Ctrl+Shift+N**; only Firefox uses **Ctrl+Shift+P**.

questions.q: The fastest way to rename a worksheet is to —
options: Double-click its tab, type the new name
questions.solution: A **double-click on the sheet tab** opens the rename box (right-click, Rename also works).

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Entrepreneur** = entre + pre + neur, from French. The ending is **-eur** (like connoisseur), and there is an r after the second p.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The patient said to the doctor, "Please prescribe a milder tablet."
options: The patient requested the doctor prescribing a milder tablet.
The patient requested the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.
The patient requested to the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.
The patient ordered the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.
questions.solution: Please → **requested the doctor to prescribe a milder tablet.** The listener follows requested directly; the verb after to stays bare. 'Requested the doctor prescribing' swaps the frame; 'requested to the doctor' inserts an impossible to; 'ordered the doctor' has a patient commanding a doctor — the tone is absurd.
questions.shortcut: please → requested + object + to + V1. Never 'to the doctor'.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Once in a blue moon
questions.solution: A blue moon (a second full moon in a month) hardly ever occurs → **very rarely**. 'Every month' and 'on a full-moon night' are literal moon options — photographable decoys.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The new trainee ___ several mistakes in his first report but corrected them quickly.
questions.solution: Mistakes are **made** (or committed). 'Did mistakes' is the commonest Indian-English slip; 'took' and 'gave' do not partner mistake at all.
questions.shortcut: make a mistake, never do a mistake.

questions.q: During the monsoon months the western side of the Western Ghats is wet, while the interior Deccan is comparatively dry. This is mainly due to:
questions.solution: Moist winds are forced up by the mountains (**orographic rainfall**) and shed rain on the windward side; the leeward side stays dry. Cherrapunji's rain is also orographic.

questions.q: Day and night on the Earth are caused by:
questions.solution: The Earth's **rotation** on its axis once in about 24 hours turns one half towards the Sun (day) and the other away (night). Revolution causes the seasons.

questions.q: The **Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)** is located at —
questions.solution: **FTII (1960)** — on the former Prabhat Studio campus in Pune.

questions.q: The **chlor-alkali process** (electrolysis of brine) produces —
options: Washing soda and bleaching powder only
questions.solution: Electrolysing concentrated brine gives **caustic soda at the cathode, chlorine at the anode and hydrogen** — the 'chlor-alkali' trio.

questions.q: If $a+b+c=0$ and $abc=8$, then the value of $a^3+b^3+c^3$ is:
questions.solution: Zero sum → $a^3+b^3+c^3 = 3abc = 24$.

questions.q: A road roller of diameter 84 cm and length 120 cm rolls 500 times over a road. The area of the road levelled is: [Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution:
The roller levels with its curved surface: $CSA=2\pi rh=2\times\frac{22}{7}\times0.42\times1.2=3.168$ sq m.

Area $=500\times3.168=1584$ sq m.
questions.shortcut: CSA in metres ($r=0.42$ m, $h=1.2$ m) is 3.168, then ×500 = 1584. Trap: 3168 doubles it; 792 halves it.

questions.q: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 12 cm is:
questions.solution: $K=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}a^2=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\times144=36\sqrt3$ sq cm.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{144}{4}=36$ → $36\sqrt3$. Trap: $24\sqrt3$ comes from the height formula $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}a$.

questions.q: What is 24% of 650?

Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out. (The letters follow English alphabetical order.)

**OPQR, UVWX, ABCD, STUV**
questions.solution: All four are four consecutive letters and each contains exactly one vowel. In OPQR, UVWX and ABCD the vowel is the **first** letter. In STUV the vowel U is third → **STUV**.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Abundant, Plentiful, Ample, Scarce**
questions.solution: Abundant, plentiful and ample all mean **more than enough**. Scarce means **too little** → **Scarce**.

questions.q: For three sets, **|A| = 25, |B| = 30, |C| = 20, |A ∩ B| = 10, |B ∩ C| = 8, |A ∩ C| = 7** and **|A ∪ B ∪ C| = 55**. How many elements are in **all three** sets?
questions.solution: 55 = 25 + 30 + 20 − 10 − 8 − 7 + x = 50 + x → x = **5**. Check: only A = 13, only B = 17, only C = 10 — no region is negative.
questions.shortcut: Rearrange the master formula for the missing term.

questions.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **no** face painted?
questions.solution: Strip one layer from every side: the unpainted core is (5 − 2)³ = 3³ = **27**.
